AI is creating a global race for power. Governments are moving quickly to build generation, grids and dedicated capacity for data centres. That urgency should extend to the energy needed by schools, hospitals, farms and businesses.

On 23 September, I will join the IEEE Tech for Sustainability Summit during New York Climate Week to discuss The Role of AI in Accelerating Energy System Innovation and Transition.

The numbers show how quickly the energy landscape is changing:

Data-centre electricity consumption could almost double between 2025 and 2030, rising from around 485 TWh to 950 TWh.

More than 100 GW of new gas capacity is planned as dedicated onsite supply for data centres. Almost all of it is in the United States, with around 13 GW announced or under development elsewhere.

Middle-income countries generate around half of ChatGPT traffic, while low- and middle-income countries host only about one-quarter of global data-centre capacity.

AI is a double-edged sword for energy systems. It can improve renewable forecasting, grid management, efficiency and investment planning. It can also drive major new electricity demand, make fossil-fuel extraction cheaper and more productive, and extend dependence on existing fuels. Policies, safeguards and financing decisions will determine which effects dominate.

I look forward to discussing how countries can shape this expansion around their own development priorities: building additional clean power, strengthening grids, protecting people and ecosystems, and ensuring that the infrastructure and value created are more widely shared.
